## My request:
시각 의미 데이터와 후보 데이터에 반영해줘. 그 다음 스킬의 최신 버전을 사용하여 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 이번에 반영한 주제가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 주제에 어울리는 랜덤한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
interpreted_intent: The requester asks for an independently chosen topic-appropriate random image test and use of the supplied reference. Topic context identifies space horror. The independent random draw selected autonomous observatory calibration. Agent-owned scene: routine machinery has made a seated humanlike arrangement above an empty observer chair; the engineer pauses at an interrupt switch because she recognizes its face-like organization. The intended experience is quiet human-machine estrangement, with real mechanical parts creating uncanny perception rather than adding impossible events at surreal=0. Compare an obvious inward-pointing telescope against a machine-built apparent observer: the latter offers a clearer relational test and a stronger cause for her directed response. At creativity=1 the coherent scene is developed with restrained local choices, not unrelated spectacle. Sensual=1 supports the portrait through intimate attention to face and hair; fetish=0 adds no specialized erotic focus. Chair, target, paddles, sensor arms, switch and gesture are all replaceable agent choices, never requester-prescribed facts. Their simultaneous legibility is planned through a face-chair-target triangle; visible support rods disambiguate the apparent figure from a second person.
subject: A portrait-guided person portrayed as an engineer beside autonomous optical equipment; role is agent-owned.
setting: An isolated orbital observatory calibration bay; concrete room is agent-owned.
event: The engineer recognizes a humanlike arrangement in machinery calibrating around an empty chair; this specific event is agent-owned.
visual_priorities: The portrait-guided face and directed attention give a human response to impersonal machinery.
The visibly empty chair and machine-mounted oval with two paddles create a physically ordinary but humanlike perceptual configuration.
The two sensor heads address that configuration, while a planetary limb beyond a pressure window establishes isolation in space.
baseline_prompt_en: A cinematic space-horror photograph of a person guided by the supplied portrait's facial and hair appearance, caught in a tense encounter in an isolated spacecraft interior. In the optical calibration bay of an orbital observatory, a short dark bob and fine separated fringe frame the engineer's face; her dark rounded eyes, soft oval facial contours, natural skin texture and slightly parted lips retain the portrait's appearance. Her individual presence stays quiet and intimate against the impersonal apparatus. She stands at the left edge of an empty observer chair, wearing a worn ivory utility jacket over a charcoal undershirt. One hand rests on the control rail with the fingertips stopped just short of a recessed red interrupt switch. Her torso has turned away from the console, and her eyes follow the apparatus over the chair, lips slightly open at the realization of what it resembles. The pale seat cushion, open lap straps and empty space above the cushion are fully exposed. Two jointed sensor arms descend from an overhead calibration gantry and aim their black optical apertures toward a matte-black oval alignment target suspended above the chair at seated head height. Two thin rectangular calibration paddles hang below the oval at shoulder width. The target and paddles together suggest a silent seated figure, while their narrow mounting rods remain plainly visible as machine parts. The apparatus has arranged an apparent observer over a chair whose actual seat is empty. Green calibration light cuts across the empty cushion, and the little sensor heads remain directed inward toward their own assembled silhouette. Behind this action, a round pressure window shows the hard blue-white curve of a planet against black space; the bolted window frame, sealed wall seams and worn handrail make the room feel inhabited but isolated. Frame her face, the empty cushion and the hanging target together in one moderately wide view, with her nearer face large enough to preserve the reference cues. A restrained 40 mm perspective from her chest height keeps the rods, apertures and chair separable. Pale instrument light grazes her cheek and catches a strand of hair; a dim amber service lamp gives the chair edge a second tone. Deep but readable shadows, cool desaturated metal, subtle grain and carefully controlled practical light support the human-machine standoff. The horror rests in ordinary equipment behaving as though it has built someone to look back at her.
